**Proposed mechanism:** Loss-of-function PSAP variant (null) —DISRUPTS→ PSAP (HGNC:9406); PSAP (HGNC:9406) —DECREASES→ Sulfatides (CHEBI:77329); Sulfatides (CHEBI:77329) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal lipid metabolism (GO:0006694); Lysosomal lipid metabolism (GO:0006694) —LEADS_TO→ Proteostasis (GO:0042724); Lysosomal lipid metabolism (GO:0006694) —LEADS_TO→ Leukodystrophy (HP:0001289); Loss-of-function SERPINA1 variant (e.g., Z allele) (null) —DISRUPTS→ SERPINA1 (HGNC:10595); SERPINA1 (HGNC:10595) —DECREASES→ Proteostasis (GO:0042724); Proteostasis (GO:0042724) —DISRUPTS→ Autophagosome-lysosome fusion (GO:0000277); Autophagosome-lysosome fusion (GO:0000277) —LEADS_TO→ Emphysema (HP:0002094); Proteostasis (GO:0042724) —LEADS_TO→ Leukodystrophy (HP:0001289). Mutations in PSAP lead to a loss of saposin B function, impairing the lysosomal degradation of sulfatides and contributing to leukodystrophy. Concurrently, mutations in SERPINA1 result in misfolded alpha-1-antitrypsin, which is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum and triggers proteasomal degradation pathways, ultimately impacting overall cellular proteostasis. The dysregulation of lysosomal function in MLD-SapB and the broader proteostasis disruption in A1ATD both converge on compromised cellular quality control mechanisms, potentially exacerbating neuronal damage or other cellular pathologies.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that genetic variants in PSAP or SERPINA1 do not lead to loss-of-function phenotypes or that the downstream pathways of lysosomal degradation and proteostasis are entirely independent in affected cell types. _(variant: High frequency (>=1%) of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in PSAP or SERPINA1 in relevant populations within gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this mechanistic overlap could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both metachromatic leukodystrophy and alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency, potentially by modulating lysosomal function or general proteostasis mechanisms.
